Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-16", "authors": [{"authorId": "2354350489", "name": "Seungyoon Woo"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Keonhee Park"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Gunhee Kim"}], "abstract": "Vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP retain zero-shot recognition ability, but their open-world use often requires task-agnostic continual learning: tasks arrive sequentially, past data are unavailable, task identity is unknown, and the backbone cannot be retrained. We argue that this setting fails VLMs through three coupled pressures beyond the stability-plasticity tradeoff: (1) modal-consistency drift, (2) representation-space interference, and (3) per-task capacity shortfall. We propose COMET (Collaborative Mixture-of-Expert Transfer) to resolve these three issues respectively as follows. A frozen teacher provides only a feature reference on a shared image-text pool; Tri-Affinity Distillation preserves image-image, text-text, and image-text geometry; and Student-Aware Cross-Expert Distillation aligns new experts with compatible prior experts so routing errors degrade gracefully. We design COMET to keep capacity and inference separate: a contextual bandit keeps or merges full per-task experts using post-training signals, while a reconstruction router selects sparse experts at test time without teacher semantics. On the X-TAIL benchmark, we show that each proposed component improves continual learning performance. COMET shows that continual vision-language adaptation can preserve multimodal geometry, coordinate accumulated experts, and allocate capacity jointly when feature reference, expert shaping, routing, and capacity control are separated by construction."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "e88b45fc55f83801607564ef0586b5c8f6653501", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.23181", "CorpusId": 293546318}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e88b45fc55f83801607564ef0586b5c8f6653501", "title": "Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-16", "authors": [{"authorId": null, "name": "He-Ming Zou"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Qi Wang"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Yi-Xiu Mao"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Yun Qu"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Yu-Yi Guo"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Ze-Yuan Liu"}, {"authorId": "2514699731", "name": "Cheng-Lin Li"}, {"authorId": "2329312643", "name": "Wei-Jie Liu"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Sai-Yong Yang"}, {"authorId": null, "name": "Xiang-Yang Ji"}], "abstract": "Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models. However, training agents over long-horizon interactions presents two challenges: using only terminal rewards makes turn-level credit assignment sparse and high-variance, while sequential mini-batch updates on a fixed rollout batch introduce policy staleness as the current policy drifts from the behavior policy. Existing approaches obtain denser credit via learned critics, process reward models, or on-policy distillation, but they rely on a value network, step-level annotations, or a stronger external teacher that increase training complexity. Meanwhile, importance sampling and clipping mitigate policy drift, but they do not specify a finite target that stops sequential updates from overshooting. In this work, we introduce TreeOPSD, a critic-free, tree-aware posterior self-distillation framework for long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning. Treating each interaction turn as a tree node, TreeOPSD branches alternative continuations from shared prefixes and recursively backs up terminal rewards into implicit turn-level credit. It then maps each credit to a closed-form, bounded teacher distribution parameterized by the likelihood ratio relative to the frozen behavior policy. Minimizing the divergence between this teacher and the student policy recovers the policy-gradient direction as the tangent at the behavior policy while bounding updates toward a finite target across sequential mini-batches. Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "13b5c6a319b9c9a55d865627c701206fcc42e3b8", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.23319", "CorpusId": 293545985}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/13b5c6a319b9c9a55d865627c701206fcc42e3b8", "title": "From Sliding Windows to Self-evolving Lifelong Memory: A Dual-perspective Survey of Memory Paradigms for Long-Horizon Robotics VLA Models", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23319, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-16", "authors": [{"authorId": null, "name": "Yong Wang"}, {"authorId": "2514665284", "name": "Bo-Yu Shen"}, {"authorId": "2514659041", "name": "Xin-Wei Zhang"}, {"authorId": "2500999440", "name": "Yi-Zhen Li"}, {"authorId": "2494879266", "name": "Ke Luo"}], "abstract": "Long-horizon robotic tasks expose a fundamental limitation of current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models because their restricted temporal context pre-vents effective accumulation and reuse of past experiences. As a result, memory has become a fundamental component for enabling embodied agents to perform long-horizon reasoning and adaptive decision-making. This survey presents a systematic taxonomy of VLA memory mechanisms based on memory scope and persistence, categorizing existing approaches into five representative paradigms and one emerging frontier. Based on this taxonomy, we compare representative VLA memory systems in terms of memory characteristics, architectural com-plexity, and open-source maturity, revealing a clear trade-off in which increasing architectural complexity is generally accompanied by decreasing open-source ma-turity. Finally, we discuss the key challenges in building full-lifecycle memory systems, including efficient memory management and lifelong knowledge evolu-tion. Overall, this survey provides a unified perspective on memory architectures for VLA agents and offers insights into the development of lifelong embodied in-telligence."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "1223114c5c124a33e4ad82085b5ddbc1dcb2ba2b", "externalIds": {"ArXiv": "2610.21974", "CorpusId": 293003548}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/1223114c5c124a33e4ad82085b5ddbc1dcb2ba2b", "title": "Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection", "venue": "", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21974, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-10-15", "authors": [{"authorId": "2055853475", "name": "Kajaree Das"}, {"authorId": "2511773881", "name": "Oliver B\u00f6se"}, {"authorId": "2218975962", "name": "Subarnaduti Paul"}, {"authorId": "2511789644", "name": "Gabriel Storch"}, {"authorId": "2267335619", "name": "Martin Mundt"}], "abstract": "Deepfake detectors safeguard against misinformation, rendering their failures as much a societal as a technical concern. As generators constantly evolve, detectors trained on static datasets miss newly arising threats, while progressive training interferes catastrophically. Yet, mitigating forgetfulness in terms of accuracy, the prevalent focus of continual learning (CL), is insufficient to reflect real-world impact. We therefore scrutinize the effects of CL methods with respect to evolving fairness. To this end, we analyze four dimensions of fairness across diverse demographics for detectors trained progressively on a chronological sequence of 11 real-world deepfake generation methods. Tracking fairness metrics over time, we expose non-trivial interplays between performance and fairness that depend on both the choice of CL algorithm and demographic intersections. We find accuracy degradation to typically exacerbate unfairness and, conversely, fairness improvements to remain scarce over time.
